subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw promise transparent abort, message injection, and continuation for harnesses that lack native same-turn steering, or keep steering capability-dependent and expose interruption as a separate operation?
rationale: Source and upstream contracts establish multiple technically valid semantics, but choosing whether OpenClaw should emulate transparent continuation changes user expectations, transcript meaning, tool-side-effect handling, and shared runtime policy.

options.title: Capability-aware steering
options.body: Use native same-turn steering where a harness supports it, retain boundary steering for Pi-style runtimes, and design explicit interruption separately with defined state semantics.

options.title: Emulate soft continuation
options.body: Abort unsupported active generations, persist partial output and tool state, append the new user message, and restart under a cross-runtime continuation contract.

options.title: Keep boundary semantics
options.body: Retain the current documented behavior and close this feature direction without adding transparent abort-and-resume emulation.

recommendation.title: Capability-aware steering
recommendation.body: Use native same-turn steering where a harness supports it, retain boundary steering for Pi-style runtimes, and design explicit interruption separately with defined state semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current user-facing steering command and documentation and have already reviewed the distinction between boundary steering and transparent continuation.
